content: 1. Indinavir affects the metabolism of drugs processed by the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative medications when necessary. 2. Suvorexant is not recommended for use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 3. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of tadalafil by altering its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Discontinue tadalafil at least 24 hours before initiating protease inhibitors (PIs), restart 7 days after PI initiation at 20 mg once daily, and increase to 40 mg once daily based on tolerability. 4. Indinavir and tamoxifen interact by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. CYP3A4 inhibition reduces the metabolism of tamoxifen to its active metabolite, N-desmethyl tamoxifen. 5. Indinavir increases tamsulosin levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the potential for increased toxicity. 6. Indinavir increases tazemetostat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of tazemetostat with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 7. Tepotinib increases indinavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the dosage of the P-gp substrate as recommended in its product labeling. 8. Indinavir increases tiagabine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 9. Indinavir increases tofacitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg once daily when coadministered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. 10. Indinavir increases tolvaptan levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 11. Tovorafenib decreases indinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of tovorafenib (a weak CYP3A4 inducer) with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious therapeutic failures. If unavoidable, monitor patients for loss of efficacy unless otherwise recommended in the CYP3A4 substrate prescribing information. 12. Indinavir increases trabectedin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., less than 14 days), administer the strong CYP3A inhibitor 1 week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue the day prior to the next trabectedin infusion. 13. Indinavir increases triazolam levels by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 14. Tucatinib increases indinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid concomitant use of tucatinib with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. 15. Indinavir increases ubrogepant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 16. Indinavir increases vemurafenib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 17. Indinavir increases vilazodone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase vilazodone plasma levels by 50%. Reduce the daily dose to 20 mg. 18. Indinavir increases vorapaxar levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 19. Voriconazole increases indinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 20. Indinavir and abacavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor patients. 21. Indinavir increases abemaciclib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites. Dose reduction of abemaciclib is required. If the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase abemaciclib to the dose prior to initiating the strong inhibitor. 22. Indinavir decreases the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor patients. New onset or exacerbation of diabetes mellitus and hyperglycemia have been reported with protease inhibitors. 23. Indinavir decreases the effects of albiglutide through other mechanisms (e.g., insulin resistance). Use caution and monitor patients. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors exist. 24. Indinavir increases almotriptan levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 25. Indinavir increases alprazolam levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 26. Indinavir increases amikacin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients. 27. Indinavir increases amitriptyline levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients. 28. Amobarbital decreases indinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 29. Indinavir increases apalutamide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 or CYP2C8 inhibitors does not require initial dosage modification; however, dose reduction may be needed based on tolerability. 30. Indinavir increases apixaban levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 31. Aprepitant increases indinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and indinavir increases aprepitant levels similarly. Use caution and monitor patients. 32. Indinavir increases aripiprazole levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 33. Armodafinil decreases indinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 34. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases indinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while indinavir increases artemether/lumefantrine levels. Use caution and monitor patients. 35. Atazanavir increases indinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor patients. 36. Indinavir increases atogepant levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. The recommended atogepant dosage is 10 mg orally once daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 37. Atorvastatin increases indinavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients. 38. Indinavir decreases atovaquone levels through an unknown mechanism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 39. Azithromycin increases indinavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients. 40. Indinavir increases the levels of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients. 41. Belzutifan decreases indinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. If coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates is unavoidable, consider increasing the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate dose according to its prescribing information. 42. Indinavir increases benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. 43. Berotralstat increases indinavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients. Monitor or titrate the P-gp substrate dose if coadministered. 44. Indinavir increases bexarotene levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 45. Indinavir increases bortezomib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 46. Bosutinib increases indinavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients. 47. Indinavir increases brentuximab vedotin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients for adverse reactions. 48. Indinavir increases brexpiprazole levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If also administered with a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose. 49. Indinavir increases bromocriptine levels by decreasing its metabolism, likely due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor patients. 50. Indinavir increases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients. 51. Indinavir increases buprenorphine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. 52. Indinavir increases buprenorphine buccal levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. 53. Indinavir increases buprenorphine subdermal implant levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor patients already on buprenorphine subdermal implants who require newly initiated treatment with CYP3A4 inhibitors for signs and symptoms of overmedication. If the dose of the concomitant CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should then be treated with a buprenorphine dosage form that permits dose adjustments. If a CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued in a patient stabilized on buprenorphine, monitor the patient for withdrawal. 54. Indinavir increases buprenorphine long-acting injection levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Patients transitioning to buprenorphine long-acting injection from transmucosal buprenorphine coadministered with CYP3A4 inhibitors should be monitored to ensure adequate buprenorphine plasma levels. Within 2 weeks, if signs and symptoms of buprenorphine toxicity or overdose occur and the concomitant CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, transition the patient back to a buprenorphine formulation that permits dose adjustments. 55. Indinavir increases buspirone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 56. Butabarbital decreases indinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 57. Butalbital decreases indinavir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 58. Indinavir increases cabazitaxel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. Avoid coadministration. 59. Indinavir affects calcifediol metabolism by altering CYP3A4 activity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. CYP450 inhibitors may inhibit enzymes involved in vitamin D metabolism (CYP24A1 and CYP27B1), potentially altering serum calcifediol levels and decreasing its conversion to calcitriol. Dose adjustment of calcifediol may be required, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intact PTH, and serum calcium concentrations should be closely monitored when initiating or discontinuing a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 60. Indinavir increases cannabidiol levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 61. Indinavir increases capmatinib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 62. Indinavir increases carbamazepine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Monitor plasma levels when used concomitantly. 63. Indinavir increases cariprazine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors requires cariprazine dose reduction. Refer to the dosage modification section in the drug monograph. 64. Cenobamate decreases indinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. 65. Indinavir increases chlordiazepoxide levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. Use alternatives if available. Consider lowering the benzodiazepine dose. 66. Indinavir increases inhaled ciclesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. There is a potential for increased toxicity, including an increased risk of Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. 67. Indinavir increases cilostazol levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 68. Indinavir increases cinacalcet levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 69. Indinavir increases citalopram levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients due to the potential for increased toxicity. 70. Clarithromycin increases indinavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients.
